cluster_name: Trump pauses 50% tariffs on Canada in last-minute deal
tldr: At headline level, 26 outlets across 15 country groups converge almost unanimously on the ECONOMIC frame — Trump paused 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days — amplifying Trump's triumphant 'we have a DEAL' framing. Carney's more cautious counter-narrative ('key work remains') surfaces in only three headline clusters (Channel News Asia, Straits Times, Reuters), while a structural dimension — Keystone XL pipeline revival tied to the deal — appears in only The Guardian's title, making it invisible at the headline layer for all other outlets.
event_summary: US President Trump announced late on 18 August 2026 a three-day pause on 50% tariffs covering approximately $20 billion of Canadian goods — including wine, hockey sticks, and cement — hours before a midnight deadline, citing a provisional deal with Prime Minister Carney's government; Carney confirmed progress but characterised the pause as a postponement rather than a completed deal.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet in the corpus to surface the Keystone XL pipeline revival in the headline — extending the economic frame beyond the tariff pause to a bilateral infrastructure and energy dimension entirely absent from all other 25 titles.

Uniquely ran a pre-outcome headline ('Trump, Canada's Carney hold talks as US tariff deadline nears') rather than announcing the pause result — placing the diplomatic process rather than the outcome as the news peg, suggesting the article predates the deal announcement.

Only outlet to use de-escalation framing ('US-Canada tariff row eases') rather than announcing the specific pause mechanism — foregrounding relational normalization over the economic event, a framing choice absent from all other titles.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, 24 outlets across 15 country groups reduce the US-Canada tariff standoff to a single ECONOMIC frame — 50% tariffs paused for three days — amplifying Trump's 'we have a DEAL' framing while suppressing Carney's 'postponement' counter-narrative to three wire/Asian headlines; the quality-of-life stakes (job losses, cost of living, vulnerable sectors) and structural deal context (USMCA renewal, dairy concessions, F-35 commitments) visible in body text are entirely absent from the headline layer.
